Not everyone knows this (I won't pretend I did), but Apple actually publishes extremely detailed dimensional drawings for dozens of devices to help accessory manufacturers design their products around them. Here are the details.

Apple hardware, presented in meticulous detail

For nearly thirty years, Jason Kottke has been one of my main sources of interesting content on the internet (and beyond), and without him I would surely miss out on a lot of treasures.

A few days ago, he published a post linking to the "Dimensional Drawings" section of the "Accessories" area on Apple's developer website.

In short, this is a repository of highly detailed technical drawings, currently covering 96 devices, including the newly released iPhone 18 Pro, Apple Watch Ultra 4 and Series 12, as well as AirPods 5.

The list also includes products like MacBook Neo and the Siri Remote, along with accessories such as AirTag, AirPods charging cases, and even the ZEISS optical inserts for Apple Vision Pro.

Each document contains precise measurements covering the overall dimensions and curvature of the device, as well as details of buttons, cameras, sensors, speakers and ports, along with detailed keepout zones indicating where specific materials cannot be placed.

Although these documents were originally created for accessory manufacturers, they will be just as fascinating for anyone with even a passing interest in hardware and industrial design, or simply for those who appreciate the meticulous approach of Apple products.

To view Apple's dimensional drawings, click this link. If you haven't yet followed kottke.org, be sure to start following it now.

Notable products on Amazon

  • Apple Watch Series 12
  • Apple Watch Ultra 4
  • AirPods Pro 3
  • AirPods 5
  • AirTag (2nd generation) — four-pack
  • MacBook Neo
  • Logitech MX Master 4
